validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, FERC-certificated, non-GEM-sourced. WBI Energy Transmission, Inc. filed for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity at FERC Docket No. CP20-52-000 on Feb 14, 2020 (confirmed independently by the docket EA itself and by a Federal Register Notice of Application, 2020/03/03, 2020-04321 -- two distinct federal publications). The FERC Environmental Assessment (EA, Dec 2020 draft, downloaded and read to exhaustion locally with pdftotext -- 21,300+ lines) Table A-2 describes 'Line Section 25 Loop' as a distinct ~20.3-mile, 12-inch-diameter new pipeline in Williams, Mountrail, and Burke Counties, ND, looping WBI Energy's existing 8-inch Line Section 25 between the Tioga Compressor Station and the new Norse Transfer Station, MAOP 1,098 psig, bi-directional. NS Energy Business's project page (independent GlobalData trade database) states the same segment as '32.67 km (=20.3 mi), 12-inch diameter, bi-directional, MAOP 1,098 psig' -- two independent sources agree on every spec. Correctly classified as a gas transmission pipeline (not gathering/distribution): it is FERC NGA section 7(c) jurisdictional interstate transmission pipe. DUPLICATE: checked against all 46 rows in this batch's roster. P3585 is one of five legitimate, physically distinct facilities of one certificated project (P3584 Tioga-Elkhorn Creek 62.8 mi/24-in, P3585 Line Section 25 Loop 20.3 mi/12-in, P3586 Line Section 30 Loop 9.6 mi/12-in, P3587 Tioga Compressor Lateral 0.5 mi/20-in, P3588 Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border 0.3 mi/24-in) -- the FERC EA's own facilities table (Table A-2) lists all five as separate pipe segments with different diameters, counties, and MAOPs, so this is not a segment double-count; each PID maps to a real, distinct piece of pipe. Not a relabel of any other roster row (P3584 is 24-in/62.8mi, clearly the same-project sibling, not the same physical pipe). STATUS: in-service since Feb 1, 2022 per WBI Energy's own release, confirmed independently by two local broadcast/public-radio outlets (KFYR-TV, 2022-02-09; Prairie Public Broadcasting, 2022-02-07), both stating the pipeline is 'now in-service'/'operational' -- 'operating' is correct and current (no evidence found of any subsequent idling, conversion, or abandonment as of this 2026 sweep). Opened and read all 8 harvested wiki citations for this page (Williston Herald headline is 404 live but its Wayback-independent content is corroborated by Minot Daily News reporting the same construction-start week; NS Energy; WBI handout PDF; FERC EA + its Wayback mirror; WBI Energy's own project page; EIA natural gas data landing page, which is a general data portal that does not itself name this project and was not used as a ref). Nothing traces to gem.wiki or GEM.

validity.recommendation: no value change -- flag for reviewer awareness only: Capacity is the whole project's incremental design capacity, restated identically on all 5 sibling rows (P3584/P3585/P3586/P3587/P3588)
validity.researcher_notes: Per the batch brief's aggregate-vs-segment rule: Capacity=250 MMcf/d is confirmed correct by two independent sources (KFYR-TV and Prairie Public Broadcasting both report 'an additional 250 million cubic feet per day', and NS Energy Business independently states 250 MMcf/d) -- but it is the PROJECT's total incremental firm transportation capacity (per the FERC EA: WBI Energy amended its application 'to provide incremental firm transportation design capacity of 250,000 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)... (a reduction of 100 MMcf/d from the original application)' -- note this EA sentence itself contains an internal unit error (250,000 MMcf/d = 250 Bcf/d is physically implausible for one project; it almost certainly should read 250,000 Dth/d, which converts to ~250 MMcf/d and matches every other source, so I did not cite this sentence's raw wording, only its underlying 250 figure as cross-checked against clean statements elsewhere), not an independently-metered figure for this specific 20.3-mile loop. Unlike a large multi-decade network (e.g. P0168 CIG's 6,920 km), this project's five new segments are literally in physical series on one continuous new corridor (receipt stations feeding into Line Section 25 Loop at its Norse end, flowing through Line Section 30 Loop and the Tioga Compressor Lateral, into the Tioga-Elkhorn Creek pipeline, to the Northern Border interconnect), so a uniform per-segment capacity is plausible engineering, not obviously wrong -- but I could not independently confirm the throughput specifically attributable to the Line Section 25 Loop segment alone (vs. the project total) from any public source (checked WBI Energy's own project page and FERC Form No. 2 was not searched -- out of scope for this pass). Recording this as a caveat per the standing aggregate-on-segment rule rather than silently passing it; the value itself is not shown to be wrong.
